correctness.rationale: For every finite field the quotient by the central line is Heisenberg. Complete classification counts subalgebras in dimensions 0–4 as 1, q^3+q^2+q+1, 2q^2+q+1, q+1, 1. All hyperplanes are ideals. Distinct line spans yield D11=q^4(q+1)^2. For each nonderived 2-plane the unique hyperplane containing it leaves q^3 nonpermutable lines, yielding D12=D21=q^4(2q+1). Plane pairs reduce to ordered projective noncentral points outside a common line through the center, yielding D22=q^3(q+1); every other dimension cell vanishes. Polynomial arithmetic gives the stated total and probability, valid including characteristic two. A standalone checker enumerates all RREF subspaces and every ordered pair over F2,F3,F4,F5 (nonprime field explicitly checked) and agrees. Limits: finite experiments are not the universal proof; the symbolic incidence argument is.

value.rationale: The subalgebra commutativity degree was introduced as a natural probabilistic Lie-lattice invariant in 2026; the four-dimensional filiform algebra is the first class-three nilpotent case in the low-dimensional taxonomy. Exact ordered failure counts by both dimensions (rather than only a scalar) reveal which strata cause nonpermutability and supply a reproducible uniform finite-field benchmark. The result also identifies the large-field decay of the invariant as 11/q^2, contrasting with existing class-two central-stabilization formulas. It uses published lattice descriptions but requires a nontrivial incidence decomposition, and is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a simple renaming of the literature.
